Everything we do at Stanburn is based on our vision for all pupils: Believe, Achieve, Succeed. This philosophy runs through everything we do, ensuring each pupil receives not only an outstanding learning offer, but a wealth of personal development opportunities that broaden horizons and develop character. We aim for every child to reach their fullest potential, removing barriers to learning and working closely with families and external professionals to ensure that all learners thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. By fostering a culture of inclusion, we empower every pupil to reach their full potential and contribute positively to our school community and beyond.

pageCache.text:
Our Vision & Values
At Stanburn, we are optimistic that every child has endless possibilities; it is our role to nurture them to believe in themselves and achieve their potential.
We pursue the highest academic standards for every child, no matter their starting point. Through our exciting and thought-provoking teaching, our children soon develop a love of learning and want to achieve their very best.
The Stanburn community really is a family. We teach our children that kindness and compassion for one another holds equal importance as academic success. Our children are polite and courteous as we explicitly teach good manners, and we celebrate and respect the rich diversity of our community.
Our vision and values guide us to ensure our children blossom into confident, polite, well-rounded young people who are proud of their achievements, feel good about who they are and have the tools to succeed in life.

Our Vision & Values

Our Values
These guiding principles are fundamental to everyone at Stanburn: mutual respect, kindness, and optimism. We are a vibrant school community where we learn about, and celebrate the wonderful differences that all our children and staff bring to our school. Our children have rich and wonderful lives ahead of them filled with opportunities. We teach our children to focus on the possibility that each day brings and, most of all, to look out and care for one another.

Our Vision
Believe Achieve Succeed - Learning without limits
Every child at Stanburn is special.
We believe that it is our duty to bring out the best in every child, through an understanding of what they need to succeed at each stage of their development. Our curriculum is carefully tailored to develop solid foundations in the earliest years, building on and enriching this year on year. We strive for academic excellence through developing our children's ability to work hard and complement this with a rich curriculum offer which includes music, sport, drama and competition.
Our children's social, emotional and mental development is of equal importance to us. Therefore, at Stanburn, we offer a bespoke wellbeing package to all our children. Every child is taught how to regulate their emotions both in and out of the classroom. We teach our children the vocabulary to articulate their feelings, including how to ask for help. We employ two full-time, trained wellbeing mentors who offer a range of support from informal chats in the playground to formalised counselling sessions.
Pupils leave us in Year 6 as well-rounded individuals, ready for the next stage of their education. We are always incredibly proud of what our children achieve and, more importantly, who they become. You can always recognise a Stanburn Star; they are confident, articulate, optimistic and kind.

Wraparound Care
Wraparound Care, Breakfast and After School Clubs are open to all children attending Stanburn Primary School upon completing the registration form.
The Breakfast Club runs from 7.40am to 8.35am charged at £6.00 per session.
The After School Club runs four sessions:
We provide support with home learning as well as offering a variety of resources and age-specific activities for the children, with a choice of indoor and outdoor activities. There is a rotation of creative activities; role play and construction and small world and board games. Balls, racquets, hoops and bikes are available for outdoor games. Please see our intent statement below.
Snacks are provided for children that stay until 4.30pm. This includes fruit, breadsticks and a biscuit.
Children booked in beyond 4.30pm are offered a healthy supper which can include pasta, jacket potatoes, wraps, yoghurt and fresh fruit.
Places are booked in advance through Arbor. We accept childcare vouchers.
All staff are DBS checked, fully qualified and first aid trained. Some of the staff are known to the children as they work for the school.

Personal Development
Having our children achieve well academically isn't enough. We want them to flourish in tomorrow's world, becoming responsible, respectful, active citizens. Our bespoke '5 for Five' programme develops a set of positive personal traits, dispositions and virtues that guides our pupils' conduct so that they reflect wisely, learn eagerly, behave with integrity and cooperate consistently well with others.

School Tours
Our headteacher, Ms D'Souza would be delighted to show you around our school. Prospective Reception parents are invited to meet her and view our facilities most Fridays at 9.00am (Sept-Jan)
To book a tour, please email admissions@stanburn.harrow.sch.uk A member of our admissions team will call you back to confirm. Alternatively, please call our Admissions Officer, Miss Calabrese on 020 8954 1423

Reading and Phonics
At Stanburn, we believe that a high quality and diverse English curriculum should develop children’s love of reading. We aim to challenge all our children to have an appreciation of a rich and varied curriculum that inspires a love of reading and develops fluent writers.
In addition to daily English lessons, children excel in early reading through the use of our synthetic phonics programme, Read, Write Inc. In KS1, the children read weekly with an adult and have regular phonics assessments to ensure rapid, embedded progress. In KS2, children read through whole class teaching (VIPERS) and specific children will be supported through extra reading. We believe it is essential for children to read as wide a range of literature as possible, so we use a range of texts including those within reading schemes, fiction and non-fiction texts, poetry and plays. We place a strong emphasis on reading comprehension and the children are taught how to read for meaning. This is reinforced through guided reading sessions. Parents are encouraged to take an active part in helping their child/ children to learn to read. Each year the children participate in World Book Day along with National Poetry Day. We also provide opportunities for creative writing competitions through the wider curriculum. This ensures that children benefit from access to positive role models from the local and wider locality.

Curriculum Intent
Our curriculum is planned and sequenced so that new knowledge and skills build on what has come before. Academic learning is underpinned by a strong emphasis on personal development and social skills so that children make and maintain healthy relationships with others. They learn responsibility and develop a sense of self so that they understand and value their place in the world.
At Stanburn, our curriculum is designed around four key principles. We call this our Curriculum VISA: it is a passport to their next destination.
Our pupils are at the centre of the curriculum and our skilled staff encourage all our children to have ownership of their learning journey. Our Stanburn Curriculum Visa ensures success for every pupil.
